book.title: Crime and Punishment
book.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky (translated by Constance Garnett)
book.notes: Partial gold: run chapters 1-11 only. Spine order: wrap0000 (cover), h-0 (Gutenberg header), h-1 (translator's preface, run ch 1), h-2 (title page 'Crime and Punishment / Part I'), h-3..h-9 (Part I ch I-VII, run ch 2-8), h-10 (opens with the heading 'PART II' and then Part II ch I, run ch 9), h-11, h-12 (Part II ch II-III, run ch 10-11). Later part headings (III-VI) sit inside their first chapter's document, as with h-10; h-42 is the Epilogue. Run ch 1 is about Dostoevsky, not the story: Petersburg is the only gold entity it names. Spell names as this translation does: Svidrigaïlov (with diaeresis), Semyon Zaharovitch, Luise Ivanovna, Dounia, Razumihin, Hay Market (two words). Entity types follow Annalist's vocabulary (character, place, organization, artifact, event, concept). Some aliases first appear after run ch 11 (Pulcheria Alexandrovna, Dmitri Prokofitch, Arkady Ivanovitch, Andrey Semyonovitch, Amalia Ivanovna, Amalia Ludwigovna); they are listed only so a run built past ch 11 still matches, and each entity's notes say where the form first appears.

entities.name: Raskolnikov
entities.notes: 'A young man' until he gives his name to the pawnbroker in ch 1. The diminutive 'Rodya' first appears in ch 3 (his mother's letter); the full 'Rodion Romanovitch Raskolnikov' first in ch 4. See identity_reveals. The bare surname belongs to him, not to his mother or sister.

entities.name: Alyona Ivanovna
entities.notes: The pawnbroker. Killed by Raskolnikov in ch 7.

entities.name: Lizaveta Ivanovna
entities.notes: Named in ch 1 ('Lizaveta's work'), where Raskolnikov also asks after the pawnbroker's sister; ch 5 first states that she is Alyona's younger sister. Killed in ch 7.

entities.name: Marmeladov
entities.notes: Sits unnamed in the tavern at the end of ch 1 ('a retired government clerk'); names himself in ch 2. This translation spells the patronymic 'Zaharovitch'. He dies in run ch 14, outside this gold.

entities.name: Katerina Ivanovna
entities.notes: Marmeladov's second wife, an officer's daughter, consumptive, with three children by her first husband.

entities.name: Sonia
entities.notes: Marmeladov's daughter by his first wife. 'Sonia' and 'Sofya Semyonovna' both appear in ch 2; 'Sonia Marmeladov' in ch 4.

entities.name: Lebeziatnikov
entities.notes: Only talked about in scope (Marmeladov's story). 'Andrey Semyonovitch' first appears in run ch 12.

entities.name: Amalia Fyodorovna Lippevechsel
entities.notes: The Marmeladovs' landlady. In scope she is only 'Amalia Fyodorovna'; 'Amalia Ivanovna' and 'Amalia Ludwigovna' first appear in run ch 14.

entities.name: Nastasya
entities.notes: Cook and only servant of Raskolnikov's lodging house. In ch 10 Razumihin calls her 'Nastasya Nikiforovna' and she corrects him: 'I am not Nikiforovna, but Petrovna.' Nikiforovna is not her name.

entities.name: Praskovya Pavlovna
entities.notes: Raskolnikov's landlady. Unnamed in ch 1 ('his landlady', to whom he owes money); named Praskovya Pavlovna in ch 3; the IOU in ch 8 makes her 'the widow of the assessor Zarnitsyn'; Razumihin calls her 'Pashenka' in ch 10.

entities.name: Natalya Yegorovna
entities.notes: The landlady's daughter, whom Raskolnikov once promised to marry; she died of typhus a year before the story. Ch 9 tells this without her name; ch 10 names her.

entities.name: Razumihin
entities.notes: Raskolnikov's old university comrade. In ch 10 he jokingly introduces himself as 'Vrazumihin'. 'Dmitri Prokofitch' first appears in run ch 16.

entities.name: Pulcheria Raskolnikov
entities.notes: Raskolnikov's mother. In scope she appears only through her letter, signed 'PULCHERIA RASKOLNIKOV'. 'Pulcheria Alexandrovna' first appears in run ch 14.

entities.name: Dounia
entities.notes: Raskolnikov's sister. 'Dounia' from ch 3; 'Avdotya Romanovna' first in ch 4. See identity_reveals.

entities.name: Svidrigaïlov
entities.notes: Only talked about in scope (the letter, Raskolnikov's thoughts). The ASCII spelling 'Svidrigailov' is accepted for matching. 'Arkady Ivanovitch' first appears in run ch 20.

entities.name: Marfa Petrovna
entities.notes: Svidrigaïlov's wife.

entities.name: Pyotr Petrovitch Luzhin
entities.notes: Dounia's fiancé. Only talked about in scope; he appears in run ch 12.

entities.name: Afanasy Ivanovitch Vahrushin
entities.notes: Merchant in the mother's town who lends against her pension and sends Raskolnikov money in ch 10. The letter first calls him 'Vassily Ivanovitch Vahrushin', then 'Afanasy Ivanovitch'; ch 4 and ch 10 say 'Afanasy Ivanovitch Vahrushin'. One person. Not Ivan Afanasyvitch, Marmeladov's superior in ch 2.

entities.name: The fat dandy
entities.notes: Unnamed gentleman stalking the drunk girl on K—— Boulevard in ch 4. Raskolnikov shouts 'You Svidrigaïlov!' at him as an insult; he is not Svidrigaïlov.

entities.name: Koch
entities.notes: One of the two callers at the pawnbroker's door during the murders; detained and then cleared in ch 8.

entities.name: Pestryakov
entities.notes: The young law student who joins Koch at the door in ch 7 ('I'm studying the law you see!') is unnamed there; ch 8 names him.

entities.name: Ilya Petrovitch
entities.notes: Assistant superintendent at the district police office. Nikodim Fomitch says 'His nickname in the regiment was the Explosive Lieutenant'. Luise Ivanovna calls him 'Mr. Captain'.

entities.name: Nikodim Fomitch
entities.notes: Superintendent of the district police. Raskolnikov addresses him as 'Captain'.

entities.name: Zametov
entities.notes: Head clerk at the police office. Ch 9 calls him only 'the head clerk' and once 'Alexandr Grigorievitch'; the surname Zametov first appears in ch 10.

entities.name: Luise Ivanovna
entities.notes: German keeper of a disorderly 'honourable house', scolded by Ilya Petrovitch in ch 8. The translation spells it 'Luise', not 'Louisa'.

entities.name: Zossimov
entities.notes: Doctor and friend of Razumihin; only talked about in ch 10 and appears in run ch 11.

entities.name: Petersburg
entities.notes: Ch 1 (the translator's preface) names it in 'the Petersburg school of Engineering'; the story is set there from ch 1. A wiki that skips the preface still passes at ch 1.

entities.name: Vassilyevsky Ostrov
entities.notes: Razumihin lives near the bridge to it (ch 4, ch 9).

entities.name: The police office
entities.notes: The district police office where Raskolnikov is summoned in ch 8. 'The police' are mentioned from ch 3 (the landlady's complaint), so an earlier page passes too.

entities.name: The axe
entities.notes: Taken from the porter's room in ch 6 after Nastasya blocks the kitchen; used in ch 7 and put back under the porter's bench. Ch 6 speaks of taking 'an axe' only in general.

entities.name: Raskolnikov's silver watch
entities.notes: His father's watch, pawned with Alyona Ivanovna in ch 1.

entities.name: Alyona Ivanovna's purse
entities.notes: Cut from her neck in ch 7; hidden with the stolen pledges under a stone in a courtyard in ch 9, unopened.

entities.name: The murder of Alyona Ivanovna and Lizaveta

ambiguities: First chapters follow the brief: the first chapter that names the entity. Two entities are the exception because the text states their ties before it names them: the landlady (ch 1, 'his landlady', to whom he owes money; named Praskovya Pavlovna in ch 3) and Natalya Yegorovna (ch 8, the dead daughter he promised to marry; named in ch 10). Marmeladov (unnamed in ch 1, named ch 2) and Pestryakov (unnamed in ch 7, named ch 8) take their naming chapter; an earlier page passes anyway.

Lizaveta and Alyona: ch 1 hints at the tie ('Lizaveta's work'; 'your sister is not here with you?') but only ch 5 states it. The relation is strict at ch 5, so a wiki that infers 'sister of' in ch 1-3 is flagged early.
Lizaveta is a 'step-sister' to the huckster's wife (ch 5) and a 'half-sister, being the child of a different mother' in ch 6. Sister, half-sister and step-sister all fall in the kin family and pass.

Vahrushin's forename: 'Vassily Ivanovitch Vahrushin' once at the start of the letter (ch 3), 'Afanasy Ivanovitch' afterwards (ch 3, 5, 11). One man. Do not confuse him with 'Ivan Afanasyvitch', Marmeladov's superior in ch 2 (not in this gold).
Ilya Petrovitch beating the landlady on the stairs (ch 9) is Raskolnikov's delirium: Nastasya says 'Nobody has been beating the landlady.' Never record it as an event or a relation.

The beating of the mare (ch 5) is a dream of Raskolnikov's childhood. Its Mikolka is a dream figure, so he is left out of this gold. Later chapters have a painter Nikolay, and ch 7 already shouts for 'Mitka', one of the painters; none of them is the dream Mikolka.
'You Svidrigaïlov!' (ch 4) is an insult to a stranger. Svidrigaïlov himself does not appear in run ch 0-10.

Raskolnikov's intent to kill the pawnbroker is first stated outright in ch 5 (the dream's aftermath and 'an old woman, on whose life an attempt was contemplated'); chs 1-4 speak only of a 'project', a 'rehearsal' and 'It'. Scorer limitation: early_relations matches word stems, so a wiki row 'plans to murder' shown in ch 5 is flagged as an early 'murdered' (ch 7). The gold uses 'murdered' rather than 'killed' so that the likelier wording 'plans to kill' does not trip it.
'Captain' is a courtesy title here: Luise Ivanovna calls Ilya Petrovitch 'Mr. Captain' and Raskolnikov calls Nikodim Fomitch 'Captain'. Not a reason to merge the two policemen.
Nastasya's patronymic: Razumihin guesses 'Nikiforovna' (ch 10); she says 'Petrovna'. Only Petrovna is hers.
'Vrazumihin' (ch 10) is Razumihin's joke on his own name, accepted as an alias but not a second person.

Name forms that first appear after run ch 10 are aliases for matching only: Pulcheria Alexandrovna (run ch 14), Dmitri Prokofitch (ch 16), Arkady Ivanovitch (ch 20), Andrey Semyonovitch (ch 12), Amalia Ivanovna and Amalia Ludwigovna (ch 14). Showing any of them as of ch 10 or earlier is a leak, but this partial gold cannot test it because the revealing quotes lie outside its chapters.
Zametov's first chapter is 9 (head clerk, 'Alexandr Grigorievitch'); his surname is a reveal at ch 10. A page titled 'Zametov' that already shows that name in ch 8 or 10 fails the reveal.
Statuses: Raskolnikov is ill and delirious from ch 8 to ch 10 but alive. Marmeladov, Katerina Ivanovna and Sonia are alive throughout scope; Marmeladov dies in run ch 14.
Spelling: the ASCII 'Svidrigailov' and 'Haymarket' are accepted as aliases because a model may drop the diaeresis or join the words; the key's names use the translation's spellings.
